subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Structure 3.2 Functional groups: classification of organic compounds

questions.q: A homologous series is a family of compounds that:
options: Share the same general formula and functional group, differing by CH2
questions.explain: Successive members differ by a CH2 unit and show a gradual trend in physical properties.

questions.q: The general formula of the alkanes is:
questions.explain: Saturated alkanes follow CnH2n+2 (e.g. C3H8, propane).

questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is:
questions.explain: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl (-OH) group; carboxylic acids contain -COOH.

questions.q: The compound CH3CH2CH2OH is named:
questions.explain: A three-carbon chain with an -OH on the first carbon is propan-1-ol.

questions.q: Alkenes are described as unsaturated because they:
questions.explain: Unsaturation means at least one C=C (or C≡C); alkanes are saturated.

questions.q: The functional group of a carboxylic acid is:
questions.explain: Carboxylic acids contain the carboxyl group -COOH (e.g. ethanoic acid, CH3COOH).

questions.q: Which is the correct molecular formula of ethene?
questions.explain: Ethene is the simplest alkene, CnH2n with n=2, so C2H4.

questions.q: Structural isomers are compounds with:
options: The same molecular formula but different structural arrangements
questions.explain: For example, butane and methylpropane share C4H10 but differ in structure.

questions.q: How many structural isomers have the molecular formula C4H10?
questions.explain: C4H10 exists as butane (straight chain) and methylpropane (branched).

questions.q: The functional group -CHO belongs to the:
questions.explain: Aldehydes have a terminal carbonyl (-CHO); ketones have the carbonyl within the chain.

questions.q: The name of the compound CH3COOH is:
questions.explain: A two-carbon carboxylic acid is ethanoic acid (acetic acid).

questions.q: Members of a homologous series show a gradual change in physical properties such as boiling point because:
options: Molecular size and intermolecular forces increase with chain length
questions.explain: Longer chains have stronger London forces, raising boiling points along the series.

questions.q: The functional group of a halogenoalkane contains a:
questions.explain: Halogenoalkanes have one or more halogen atoms replacing hydrogen.

questions.q: Which compound is a member of the same homologous series as propan-1-ol?
questions.explain: Ethanol and propan-1-ol are both alcohols (-OH), members of the same series.

questions.q: The molecular formula C3H6O could represent:
questions.explain: C3H6O corresponds to the aldehyde propanal and the ketone propanone, which are functional-group isomers.

questions.q: The suffix '-oic acid' in an organic name indicates the presence of a:
questions.explain: IUPAC uses '-oic acid' for carboxylic acids, '-ol' for alcohols and '-al' for aldehydes.

questions.q: An ester is formed by reacting a carboxylic acid with:
questions.explain: Esterification of an acid and an alcohol (with an acid catalyst) produces an ester and water.

questions.q: How many carbon atoms are in a molecule of butanoic acid?
questions.explain: 'But-' indicates a four-carbon chain; the acid carbon is included in the count.

questions.q: Compared with alkanes, alkenes are more reactive because:
options: The C=C double bond is a region of high electron density open to attack
questions.explain: The pi electrons of the double bond make alkenes react readily, e.g. in addition reactions.

questions.q: Which is the correct name for CH3CH2CHO?
questions.explain: A three-carbon chain ending in -CHO is the aldehyde propanal.
